title: The regular singular inverse problem in differential Galois theory: the specialization lemma for regular singular equations (Lemma 2.13)
author: Thomas Serafini, Michael Wibmer
work: The regular singular inverse problem in differential Galois theory
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Lemma 2.13 (source0.tex lines 666-668, printed as Lemma 2.13 on page 9 of the published version), the global specialization lemma on which the paper's main theorem rests: for algebraically closed k subset k', a set S of d+1 points of P^1(k) and a matrix A over k'(z) whose equation has all poles in S, is Fuchsian at the first d points and regular singular at the last one, there is a finitely generated k-subalgebra B of k' and a monic f in B[z] with A in B[z]_f such that every k-specialization of B preserves all three properties. The retained complete proof (lines 670-743) is a genuine 74-line argument, not a routine verification: it must build the finitely generated algebra from the coefficients after clearing the poles, control the behaviour at infinity through the coordinate change t = 1/z, transport the local result through a translation of the singular point, track the localization B[t]_f through the specialization, and then redo the argument in the two cases where infinity belongs to S or is only regular singular. The residual difficulty is that the specialization must preserve a mixture of global pole conditions and local Fuchsian/regular-singular behaviour simultaneously, which is research-level differential Galois theory well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.

primary.theorem: Lemma 2.13 (global specialization of regular singular equations)
